findings.name: Enabled policy with no assigned users or groups
findings.description: An enabled Conditional Access policy applies to no users or groups, making it ineffective.
findings.remediation: Assign the policy to the intended user or group scope, or disable/delete it if obsolete.

findings.name: Excluded groups in Conditional Access policy
findings.description: The policy excludes one or more groups. Exclusions are a common source of security gaps if not documented and reviewed regularly.
findings.remediation: Verify the exclusion is still required. Document the business justification. Review quarterly.

findings.name: Privileged roles not covered by MFA-requiring policy
findings.description: One or more privileged directory roles are NOT covered by a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA.
findings.remediation: Create or update a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all privileged directory roles.

findings.name: Break-glass account not properly excluded
findings.description: No break-glass account was detected in the exclusion list of MFA-requiring policies.
findings.remediation: Designate 1-2 cloud-only break-glass accounts, exclude them from all Conditional Access policies, and monitor their sign-in activity closely.

findings.name: Wide exclusion group (more than 20 members)
findings.description: A group with more than 20 members is excluded from a Conditional Access policy.
findings.remediation: Review group membership. Tighten to only the users who genuinely need the exclusion.

findings.name: No enabled policy blocks legacy authentication
findings.description: No enabled Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication protocols (Exchange ActiveSync, other clients). Legacy auth bypasses MFA entirely.
findings.remediation: Create a CA policy targeting legacy client app types with a Block grant control.

findings.name: Insufficient or absent CA enforcement
findings.description: Tenant has zero enabled CA policies, or fewer than 3, indicating no meaningful Conditional Access enforcement.
findings.remediation: Enable baseline policies: require MFA for admins, block legacy auth, require MFA for all users.

findings.name: Conflicting Conditional Access policies
findings.description: Two enabled policies target overlapping users/apps with contradictory grant controls (block vs require MFA).
findings.remediation: Review both policies. Consolidate or narrow scope to avoid ambiguity.

findings.name: Admin policy uses weak authentication strength
findings.description: A policy targeting privileged roles uses an authentication strength weaker than phishing-resistant MFA.
findings.remediation: Upgrade the authentication strength to phishing-resistant (FIDO2, certificate-based, or Windows Hello for Business).

findings.name: Named location used in policy requires review
findings.description: A Conditional Access policy uses named or excluded locations. These require periodic review as IP ranges and country memberships change.
findings.remediation: Review named locations quarterly. Confirm no stale or overly broad entries.
